page: Vultr voc-c-8c-16gb-150s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor with an x86_64 architecture. The instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with 150 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing the server in the top 25% of its class. Multi-core performance, measured by stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth is also average, delivering 123.16 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 72.22 GB/sec for large block write operations. The server demonstrates average performance in database operations, static web serving throughput at 8.57 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations at 15.55 million operations per second. However, a performance tradeoff is visible in LLM inference tasks; while prompt processing for a small 135M model is average, prompt processing for a medium 7B model is weak, falling into the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and NVMe storage bundle offer a balanced resource profile for compute-focused workloads without the overhead of high-capacity memory configurations. This server is well-suited for applications requiring dedicated, predictable CPU performance with moderate memory needs. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, database operations, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and general-purpose compute workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or GPU acceleration.
